title: Apple: from a garage to $5 trillion
dek: Fifty years of Apple: the founding, the boardroom fight that pushed Steve Jobs out, his return, the iPhone, the Tim Cook years and the new CEO.
seoTitle: The Apple story: a timeline from 1976 to John Ternus
bigLabel: Market value at the 9 Nov 2026 close

glance.what: Apple was founded in a California garage in 1976. Steve Jobs was pushed out in 1985, came back in 1997 when the company was struggling, and led it through the iPod, iPhone and iPad. Tim Cook ran it from 2011 to 2026, and John Ternus took over on 1 September 2026.
glance.why: Apple's products changed how people use computers, music and phones, and it is now the world's most valuable company. Its history also includes a founder who was pushed out and later came back to lead a recovery.
glance.next: Ternus faces questions about Apple's place in AI and how well the foldable iPhone Duo sells. Cook stays on as executive chairman.

forYou: If you use an iPhone, iPad or Mac, the decisions on this timeline shaped them: the Mac's windows and mouse, the iPod's move into music, the App Store's model for apps, and Apple's own chips.
next: How the iPhone Duo sells and what Apple does in AI under Ternus.

events.title: Apple is founded in a garage
events.summary: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ron Wayne start Apple Computer Company as a partnership in the Jobs family garage in Los Altos, California. Their first product is the Apple I, a circuit board Wozniak designed for hobbyists. Wayne pulls out 11 days later.

events.title: Apple becomes a company, with an investor's backing
events.summary: After investor Mike Markkula agrees to back the two Steves and writes their business plan, Apple Computer, Inc. is incorporated.

events.title: The Apple II arrives
events.summary: Jobs and Wozniak show the Apple II at the first West Coast Computer Faire in San Francisco. Unlike the Apple I, it comes in a plastic case with a keyboard and colour graphics, and it becomes Apple's first big hit.
events.differs: The fair opened on 16 April; some accounts, such as Cult of Mac's, date the Apple II's debut to 17 April, the fair's second day.

events.title: A visit to Xerox shapes the future
events.summary: Jobs visits the Xerox PARC research lab and sees a computer controlled with windows, icons and a mouse. He decides Apple's next computers must work the same way.

events.title: Apple goes public
events.summary: Apple sells shares on the stock market for the first time, at $22 each, raising more than $100 million. Jobs and Wozniak become millionaires overnight.

events.title: The Lisa flops, and Apple hires a boss from Pepsi
events.summary: Apple launches the Lisa, one of the first personal computers with a mouse and on-screen windows. At $9,995 it fails to sell. In 1983 Apple also recruits PepsiCo president John Sculley as chief executive, partly to mentor the young Jobs.

events.title: The Macintosh, launched with the '1984' ad
events.summary: Jobs unveils the Macintosh, which brings the mouse and on-screen windows to more people at about a quarter of the Lisa's price. It is launched with a TV ad called '1984'.

events.title: Steve Jobs is pushed out of Apple
events.summary: After the Mac sells poorly, Sculley strips Jobs of his duties in April and defeats his attempt to take back control in May. Jobs resigns in September and starts a new computer company, NeXT. Wozniak had already left in February 1985.

events.title: The PowerBook sets the shape of the modern laptop
events.summary: Apple's PowerBook pushes the keyboard back towards the screen, leaving room for palm rests and a pointing device in front. Most laptops still follow this layout.

events.title: The Newton stumbles and Sculley is replaced
events.summary: Apple's first handheld computer, the Newton MessagePad, has a troubled launch. It contributes to Sculley being replaced as chief executive by Michael Spindler in 1993.

events.title: Apple buys NeXT, and Jobs comes back
events.summary: Struggling to build a modern operating system of its own, Apple agrees to buy NeXT for $400 million. Jobs returns as an adviser to chief executive Gil Amelio, who had taken over earlier in 1996. NeXT's software later becomes the basis of Mac OS X.
events.differs: Apple announced the deal at $400 million. The UK's Centre for Computing History says it completed on 7 February 1997 for $427 million in cash and stock; other accounts give 4 February.

events.title: The board pushes out Gil Amelio
events.summary: With Apple losing money and its shares at a 12-year low, the board removes Amelio as chief executive. Jobs takes on a bigger role with the board and management.

events.title: Microsoft invests $150 million in Apple
events.summary: On stage at Macworld in Boston, Jobs announces a deal with long-time rival Microsoft. It buys $150 million of Apple shares and commits to making Office for the Mac for five years. Some of the crowd boos when Bill Gates appears on the big screen. Apple's shares rose 33% that day.
events.status: Confirmed · The Motley Fool, Mac History

events.title: Jobs becomes interim CEO
events.summary: Twelve years after he was forced out, Jobs is named Apple's interim chief executive. He cuts most of the product line to focus on a handful of computers.

events.title: The iMac starts the comeback
events.summary: Jobs unveils the iMac, a colourful all-in-one computer built for getting online. It goes on sale on 15 August 1998 and becomes the best-selling Mac of all time; Apple returns to profit that year.
events.status: Confirmed · Centre for Computing History, Britannica

events.title: Mac OS X replaces the old Mac software
events.summary: Apple releases Mac OS X, built on NeXT's technology. It becomes the foundation for the software that runs Macs, iPhones and iPads today.

events.title: The iPod: '1,000 songs in your pocket'
events.summary: Apple unveils the iPod, a $399 music player that stores up to 1,000 songs and syncs with the iTunes software on a Mac. It marks Apple's move beyond computers.

events.title: The iTunes Music Store sells songs for 99 cents
events.summary: Apple opens an online store selling single songs for 99 cents each with no subscription, at first only to US customers on Macs.

events.title: Macs switch to Intel chips
events.summary: Apple announces it will move the Mac from PowerPC chips to Intel's, citing speed and energy use. The first Intel Macs arrive in January 2006.

events.title: Jobs unveils the iPhone, and 'Computer' is dropped from Apple's name
events.summary: Jobs introduces the iPhone, a touchscreen phone, iPod and internet device in one, priced at $499 and $599 in the US. Apple Computer also renames itself Apple Inc. The iPhone goes on sale on 29 June 2007.

events.title: The App Store opens with 500 apps
events.summary: Apple lets outside developers sell apps for the iPhone. The App Store opens with 500 apps, a day before the iPhone 3G goes on sale.

events.title: The iPad
events.summary: Apple announces the iPad tablet, which runs the same apps as the iPhone on a bigger screen. It goes on sale in the US on 3 April 2010.

events.title: Jobs steps down; Tim Cook becomes CEO
events.summary: Jobs resigns as chief executive and recommends chief operating officer Tim Cook as his successor. The board names Cook CEO and Jobs chairman.

events.title: Steve Jobs dies at 56
events.summary: Jobs dies in Palo Alto, California, after a long fight with pancreatic cancer, six weeks after stepping down.

events.title: Apple Watch opens a new product category
events.summary: The Apple Watch goes on sale. Sales start slowly but grow once Apple focuses it on fitness and health.

events.title: Apple becomes the first $1 trillion US company
events.summary: Apple becomes the first publicly traded US company valued at $1 trillion. It passes $2 trillion on 19 August 2020.
events.status: Market data · PYMNTS, Computer History Museum

events.title: Macs move to Apple's own chips
events.summary: The first Macs with Apple-designed M1 chips arrive, after Apple announced in June that it would stop using Intel's chips.

events.title: Briefly worth $3 trillion, a first for any company
events.summary: Apple's shares touch $182.88, making it the first company ever valued at $3 trillion, though only briefly during the day.

events.title: Vision Pro headset, then Apple Intelligence
events.summary: Apple releases the Vision Pro mixed-reality headset at about $3,500. In June it announces Apple Intelligence, its AI features. Both get mixed reviews, and Apple is widely viewed as trailing rivals in AI, Invezz reports.

events.title: Apple touches $4 trillion
events.summary: Strong demand for the iPhone 17 pushes Apple's market value above $4 trillion for the first time during trading, making it the third company to get there after Nvidia and Microsoft. It closed just below, at about $3.99 trillion.

events.title: Apple turns 50
events.summary: Apple marks 50 years since its founding with a letter from Tim Cook titled '50 Years of Thinking Different' and events in its stores.

events.title: Tim Cook says he will step down; John Ternus named next CEO
events.summary: Apple announces that Cook, CEO for 15 years, will hand over to hardware engineering chief John Ternus on 1 September and become executive chairman. AP reports Apple's market value rose by more than $3.6 trillion under Cook, from $350 billion in August 2011 to about $4 trillion.
events.status: Confirmed · Apple, via AP and Macworld

events.title: John Ternus takes over as CEO
events.summary: Ternus, 51, who has spent about 25 years at Apple, becomes chief executive. Cook moves to executive chairman.
events.status: Confirmed · Apple, via iPhone in Canada

events.title: Ternus's first launch: the foldable iPhone Duo
events.summary: At his first product event as CEO, Ternus unveils the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable phone, from $1,999. It ships on 23 October. CBS News reports new iPhone prices rose partly because of a global shortage of memory chips.

events.title: First close above $5 trillion
events.summary: Apple ends a trading day worth more than $5 trillion for the first time. Only Nvidia had done so before, in October 2025. Apple had briefly touched $5 trillion during trading on 28 July.

events.title: Record share price as Apple stays the world's most valuable company
events.summary: After record September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, reported on 2 November, Apple's shares close at a record $350.69, valuing it at about $5.1 trillion, the most of any company in the world, per 24/7 Wall St.
